{{inline |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''algebra bundle''' is a [[fiber bundle]] whose [[fiber (mathematics)|fiber]]s are [[algebra over a field|algebra]]s and [[local trivialization]]s respect the algebra structure. It follows that the [[Transition map|transition functions]] are [[algebra isomorphism]]s. Since algebras are also [[vector space]]s, every algebra bundle is a [[vector bundle]].

Examples include the [[tensor-algebra bundle]], [[exterior bundle]], and [[symmetric bundle]] associated to a given [[vector bundle]], as well as the [[Clifford bundle]] associated to any Riemannian vector bundle.
